title: adaptive oncall prober and priority snapshot sampler
author: Claire Nguyen
commit_summary: feat: add lightweight oncall prober CLI and server-side scheduler
feat: implement priority snapshot sampler with adaptive sampling rate
chore: add docs and example runbooks referencing probe outputs
test: add deterministic tests for sampler edge cases
fix: ensure probe timeouts propagate to tracing spans
description: Motivation: on-call teams need lightweight, targeted telemetry during early triage windows without overwhelming storage or noise budgets. This PR introduces an adaptive oncall prober and a prioritized snapshot sampler that together provide concise, high-signal telemetry bundles for pagers and automated runbooks. Changes in this PR: 1) prober CLI (cli/prober/runner.py) - small binary to run health checks, flame-probes, and short traces against service endpoints with pluggable collectors; 2) server scheduler (server/scheduler/probe_scheduler.go) - schedules probes during incident windows and integrates with Linear/SRE signals to raise priority; 3) snapshot sampler (server/sampler/snapshot_sampler.go & pkg/telemetry/prioritizer.go) - collects compact telemetry slices (logs, top traces, metric deltas) with adaptive sampling rates based on incident severity and recent noise; 4) oncall playbook examples and docs (docs/oncall-probes.md, examples/) - shows how to wire prober output into runbook templates and to trigger automated mitigations; 5) tests and CI updates. Backwards compatibility: prober output format is backwards-compatible with existing snapshot importers; sampler exposes opt-in new priority tags. Security note: probes are rate-limited and respect tenant RBAC; on-prem installer respects private mode. How it works: the scheduler receives a low-footprint incident signal (pager or synthetic alert) and starts the prober with a tuned budget. Probes emit compact spans and metrics that the sampler consumes; the sampler uses a priority score function (recent error rate, alert severity, service criticality, and cadence) to decide whether to store full traces or only compact summaries. Adaptive behavior reduces sampling when noise is high and increases capture when signal is concentrated. Migration: default sampling rates are conservative; operators can opt in to aggressive capture via console flags or configmaps. Testing: included unit and integration tests and an e2e scenario that simulates a spike and verifies prioritized snapshots are captured. Notes: this PR focuses on operational ergonomics (smaller bundles, better prioritization) rather than heavy payload capture; follow-ups will add richer replay hooks and retention policies. Related: ENG-2390 tracks the console integration; SRE-412 documents incident playbook templates.
review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Can the sampler be configured per-tenant? I want to ensure enterprise customers can set stricter budgets. — Author reply: Yes, sampler supports tenant-level overrides via configmap and the private installer exposes the flag.

Asha Patel: The scheduler may start too many probes during flapping incidents; can we debounce at the scheduler layer? — Author reply: Added a debounce window with exponential backoff and unit tests to cover flapping behavior (see scheduler changes).

Marco Rivera: CI flaked on one e2e job on first run; can we split the e2e into a lighter smoke test so PRs are not blocked? — Author reply: Split e2e into smoke and heavy; smoke runs on PR and heavy runs nightly.
release_notes: Add adaptive oncall prober and prioritized snapshot sampler: lightweight probes for incident triage, adaptive sampling to reduce noise, new CLI and scheduler, conservative defaults, tenant overrides available.
